The direct object of the Aktiv (den Motor, Akkusativ) becomes the subject in the Passiv (der Motor, Nominativ).
⚠ Only verbs with an Akkusativ object work this way. With verbs taking Dativ the object keeps its case: Man hilft **dem Kind** → **Dem Kind** wird geholfen. Not “Das Kind wird geholfen”.
### Who does it – von + Dativ
Most often the agent is not named at all: it is not important, otherwise there would be no point in the Passiv.
Der Motor wird **vom** Mechaniker montiert. – The engine is assembled by the mechanic. (von + dem = vom)
### The Passiv exists in every tense
The tense is set by the form of werden, the voice – by the Partizip II at the end.
tense | example |
Präsens | Der Motor wird montiert. |
Präteritum | Der Motor wurde montiert. |
Perfekt | Der Motor ist montiert worden. |
Futur I | Der Motor wird montiert werden. |
💡 In the last line there are two werden in a row: the first shows the future, the second – the Passiv.
### Perfekt: worden, not geworden
In the Passiv the prefix ge- drops out. The form geworden occurs only with the ordinary verb “to become”.
Der Motor ist montiert worden. – The engine has been assembled.
Ich bin Arzt geworden. – I became a doctor.
### How to translate it into English [collapse]
The German Passiv usually becomes an English passive with be, or an impersonal sentence with they.
Der Motor wird montiert. – The engine is being assembled. Or: they are assembling the engine.
A word-for-word “the engine becomes assembled” is a calque, English does not say it that way.
### Process against result
werden + Partizip II – a process, going on right now. sein + Partizip II – a result, already finished. Both constructions are normal.
Der Motor **wird** montiert. – the engine is being assembled, the work is going on.
Der Motor **ist** montiert. – the engine is assembled, the work is finished.
Die Wäsche ist gewaschen. / Das Auto ist repariert.
r0066.noteEn:
⚠ werden + Partizip II – this is the Passiv, werden + infinitive – the future.
The future is covered in r0065, Partizip II – in r0015, Perfekt – in r0022.
r0066.examplesEn:
Der Mechaniker montiert den Motor. – The mechanic assembles the engine.
Der Motor wird montiert. – The engine is being assembled.
Der Motor wird von dem Mechaniker montiert. – The engine is assembled by the mechanic.
Der Motor wurde montiert. – The engine was being assembled.
Der Motor ist montiert worden. – The engine has been assembled.

r0067.title: Условие без wenn: Sollte …, müsste …
r0067.titleEn: A condition without wenn: Sollte …, müsste …
r0067.content_md_en:
[sub] wenn is thrown out — its work is taken over by the position of the verb
### Two forms of one condition
A Nebensatz with wenn sends the verb to the end. If wenn is removed, the condition does not go anywhere — it begins to be marked by the verb itself, which has moved to first position.
Wenn keine Lösung gefunden wird, muss ich kündigen.
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden, müsste ich kündigen.
💡 Why this is read unambiguously: in an ordinary declarative sentence the first position is taken by the subject or by an adverbial, and the verb stands second. A verb in first position is a question without a question word, an order, this very condition, or an exclamation of wish (Hätte ich doch mehr Zeit!). None of them can be confused with a statement.
### sollte — this is «if by any chance», not «must»
There is no modal obligation here. This is the Konjunktiv II of sollen, and it marks the case as hypothetical.
Wenn keine Lösung gefunden wird – if no solution is found. An ordinary condition, without any estimate of probability.
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden – if by any chance no solution is found. The speaker allows that it may not come to that.
### The Konjunktiv in the consequence softens
muss ich kündigen – I terminate. This is an ultimatum.
müsste ich kündigen – I would have to terminate. This is a possibility out of which there is a way.
⚠ The politeness rule in German letter writing is simple: the further the form is from fact, the softer it sounds. The Konjunktiv moves what is said into the area of the possible and leaves the addressee a way out. There is no obligation here: the main clause stands quite calmly in the indicative or in the imperative – Sollten Sie Fragen haben, melden Sie sich gern.
### Why this construction uses the passive [collapse]
gefunden werden means «will be found», not «you will find». The agent is not named, and this is done on purpose.
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden – if no solution is found. Nobody is to blame.
Sollten Sie keine Lösung finden – if you do not find a solution. The same condition, but the finger is already pointing at the addressee.
r0067.noteEn:
⚠ sollte in a condition is not «must», but the Konjunktiv II with the meaning «if by any chance».
Verb order in the Nebensatz is dealt with in r0029, the Konjunktiv of modal verbs — in r0032 and r0045.
r0067.examplesEn:
Sollte keine Lösung gefunden werden, müsste ich den Vertrag kündigen. – If no solution is found, I would have to terminate the contract.
Sollten Sie Fragen haben, melden Sie sich gern. – If you have any questions, please get in touch.
Sollte es regnen, bleiben wir zu Hause. – If by any chance it rains, we will stay at home.
Wenn keine Lösung gefunden wird, muss ich kündigen. – When no solution is found, I terminate the contract.
Hätte ich mehr Zeit, würde ich helfen. – If I had more time, I would help.
